correctness.rationale: The exact identity \(H(Fp)-H(p)=(x-c)^2+(\alpha-\alpha_{\mathrm{SN}})\) is reconstructed symbolically and verified in 498 exact-rational finite tests. The affine height yields a strict positive minimum increment above the fold and the explicit N-step cube upper bound and the positive linear lower bound on the escaping orbit norm; bounded forward orbits at equality have summable squares and converge to (c,c,c). Monotone height on a bounded entire orbit has equal limits at both ends and therefore no nonzero increments. Invertibility for delta>0 makes any compact two-sided invariant set the fixed singleton. Integration against compactly supported invariant measures gives the exact moment law. Below the fold both fixed points exist. All quantities and boundary equality are proved, not extrapolated from tests.

originality.rationale: The originating 2022 paper gives the fixed-point discriminant and bounds on bounded two-sided orbits, but does not state the global fold equivalence for all bounded forward orbits, convergence of every bounded forward orbit at the saddle-node, triviality of all compact two-sided invariant dynamics there, the stationary centered second-moment identity, or the explicit post-fold cube exit budget. The key comparison is implication, not title matching. The 1997 quadratic-volume-preserving result requires a positive-definite form (rather than the present one-square semidefinite form) and only bounds the location of bounded orbits. The 2018 local-fold paper has a different quadratic placement. Search results on planar Hénon and other quadratic flows supply no theorem on these three-dimensional forward orbits. Priority uncertainty from possible unindexed general recurrence results remains.

value.rationale: The published dynamics includes invariant circles and other periodic/chaotic attractors, so a local saddle-node criterion alone cannot exclude bounded nonfixed dynamics. The global exact phase boundary for every bounded forward orbit, critical complete-orbit rigidity, stationary quadratic shell and finite residence budget settle a natural dynamical gap in the full three-dimensional family. The theorem is exact and structural, not a small numerical parameter gain or arbitrary special slice. No all-parameter classification below the fold or optimal escape-rate assertion is made.
